Version: 1.5.0
Imported: CMakeLists.txt, Common/, EGoTouchService/, LICENSE, README.md.
Local integration: HubParentGuard.h and ServiceShell.cpp parent lifetime guard;
isolated system-state event namespace; service name OpenEGoHubThpHost.
Tools are disabled. Upstream active stylus support is experimental/disconnected;
this integration does not claim to restore it.
CMake adjustment: use /clang:-ffp-contract=off with clang-cl so the upstream no-FMA requirement is applied.
0.5.4 integration fix: permit bounded initialization with a powered panel and zero
burst register; acknowledge SCM startup only after a master frame and VHF readiness.

0.5.5 policy: never restore OEM input, including parent crash and readiness failure.
0.5.6 integration: read the SYSTEM supervisor's PenHoverChannel before runtime start
and every 200 ms. Filter final VHF stylus bytes after eraser transforms: tip-up hover
becomes an out-of-range neutral report; actual tip contact is preserved. Disabling
an active hover flushes it immediately without interrupting an active stroke.
0.5.7: preserve finger mapping without fresh master data; skip corrupt slave input;
bound consecutive corrupt/zero frames before the both-invalid early return. Keep an
encoded HID contact ledger for explicit ups and partial-write recovery, serialize
flush with dispatch, correct eraser hover/absent states, and skip redundant neutral
pen writes. No active motion/pressure coalescing or extra release debounce.

0.5.8: revert redundant-neutral suppression after user-observed visual stutter.
Restore per-valid-frame pen cadence, update touch state once on success, cache active
contact count, and skip repeated ready checks after startup. Add aggregate active
frame/read/solve/send timings; no raw input or application data is logged. Existing
continuity and explicit-release fixes remain; no extra coordinate filtering/batching.

0.5.9: replace process-wide REALTIME/HIGH with NORMAL and boost only the input
worker one step; log actual scheduling. Normalize reported raw Down/Move/pending-lift
events as continuing contact in Core::TouchAt; preserve internal Report semantics
and initial-down debounce. Repeated tap and actual Windows scheduling tests added.

0.5.10: halve small-finger edge-safe margins, retaining shape/ratio checks and
large-object/palm handling. Replace whole-frame clearing on any lift in TsaOut with
per-contact pruning. Add a real TsaCore-library regression target covering 100
overlapping tap transitions through mapper/HID output and multi-finger continuity.

0.5.12: bounded, default-off raw/filter/HID contact-state tracing (no coordinates)
located a 50 ms Windows grip admission wait swallowing short taps. Reduce this to
8 ms only for quiet, confirmed, small fingers with no grip/palm/exception markers.
Preserve noise, initial debounce, explicit grip and large-contact paths. Extend the
real-library regression test to check admission and all protection exceptions.

0.5.13: user-requested removal of the remaining 8 ms grip admission delay for
already-confirmed quiet small non-palm fingers. All prior guard conditions remain;
initial debounce, noise/palm safeguards, release rules and scan cadence are unchanged.
Real-core tests require immediate confirmed Down/Move admission and guard retention.

0.5.14: after a visual-stutter regression report, restore the user-validated
0.5.12 8 ms guarded finger admission threshold. This is a mitigation; internal
timing did not establish causality. Skip redundant matrix/suffix decoding in
production solver mode, retain diagnostics/parser-only decoding and per-frame
touch/neutral-pen reports. Hardware visual validation remains required.

0.5.15: equivalent-output stylus matrix optimization: reject unobservable results
before expansion, clear only previously written ranges and use exact ARM64 integer
vector copies for interior/clipped windows. Preserve legacy anchor boundaries.
Hub headless Release omits unused GUI log copies; file logs and Debug retained.
16,000 mixed frames matched the archived 0.5.14 metadata and all returned cells;
new dense-oracle device-free test checks cached ranges. Input cadence, 8 ms finger
admission, filtering, palm/noise guards and neutral pen reports remain unchanged.

0.5.40: take a fresh power snapshot after probing the panel and use its epoch
for chip initialization. The MCU event worker waits for active frame and HID
readiness before the existing pen handshake. It gives each wake or transport
reopen three attempts, checks deadlines on reads and timeouts, and only marks
the handshake complete after the protocol parameters are written successfully.
The user reported continuous pen drags becoming repeated taps after long sleep.

0.5.41: defer an explicit MCU parameter request received before readiness.
Once awake, respond to a valid request even if the screen-status reply arrived
out of order or the host's active retry window already ended.
